x: Ted Smith was our first man home in (10th) followed by McMullen, Checkley and Newson, 12th, 15th and 16th. We thus finished 2nd in the Scratch Race despite not having our 2 Olympic men.
Ted Smith,showing his true form,was 4th,Syd James 12th, Checkley 5th.McMullen 7th and Newson 13th.After this we can hope to regain the Berman Cup in our own Open on Nov24th.

Ted Smith was our great hope for the individual title and at two miles had a lead of afew yards over the field. From the three mile point however, he must have become very tired at the sight of Met vests for he found himself walking with six or seven of their men from then on.
E.A.Smith put up his best performance of the season when finishing second in the London Business Houses 2 miles Championship at Hurlingham in the good time of 14m.28.4s.

In a ten miles invitation track walk at the White City on 31st of August Stan Vickers and Eric Hall Finished first and second in 74m.31.4s. and 76m9s. respectively. Also taking part were George Checkley who finished 15th in 83m.46s., and E.A.
1, K.J.Matthews(Royal Sutton Coldfield) 51m.39s; 2, E.W.Hall (Bel) 52.09; 6, N.Milsum(Bel)55.20; 8, E.A.Smith(Bel)55.43; 25, J.G.Coleman(Bel)59.58.

The same day (Jan.4th) E.A.Smith finished third in the London Business Houses 7 mile championship in 55.52. We also had a match versus Met.Police at "The Warren" Hayes and in a field of eighteen Stan Vickers was first home in 56.05.
…, beating Highgate, Polytechnic and many other fancied clubs in the process. A particularly fine effort was that of Ted Smith in finishing fourth and George Checkley sixth.…
